title: A chemically and thermally resolved map of Earth’s deep interior

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a global three-dimensional model that distinguishes major variations in temperature and chemical composition inside Earth, with enough spatial detail and quantified uncertainty to test competing geological explanations. Seismic tomography already maps variations in how waves travel through the interior. The breakthrough would be to determine more reliably what those variations mean physically: which reflect hotter or colder material, which reflect different compositions, and which arise from changes in mineral structure.

This would require combining observations and physical models whose sensitivities differ, including seismology, mineral physics, geochemistry and potentially neutrino measurements of broad density structure. A successful model would identify which properties the evidence separately constrains and where several explanations remain possible. Core light elements and the composition and origin of large low-shear-velocity provinces are possible targets within this larger mapping capability; they are not separate demonstrations that the capability has been achieved.

significance.text: The potentially revolutionary advance would be a stronger ability to distinguish geological explanations that fit similar seismic observations. Separating thermal and chemical contributions could make interpretations of deep reservoirs, recycled crust and mantle buoyancy more discriminating. This matters because errors in inferred temperature propagate into estimates of density and buoyancy and into attempts to reconstruct mantle evolution. The significance is a conditional scientific judgment, rather than a demonstrated outcome or a source-established historical ranking.

Better constraints on core chemistry could also sharpen accounts of Earth's accretion, core formation and the conditions that sustain its magnetic field. The 2021 core-composition review connects those questions to the identity and abundance of light elements in the core. A global map would contribute to these investigations, but resolving composition would not automatically select a unique history of Earth's formation.

Synthesis: composition and temperature maps would provide inputs to broader explanations, rather than directly measuring every process of interest. Reconstructing material movement would additionally require dynamical constraints. Estimating deep heat flow would require thermal transport properties and boundary conditions. The map would remain an inference from observations and physical models, would not supply direct samples of the deep interior, and would not by itself enable reliable earthquake or volcanic-eruption forecasts.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved capability is a sufficiently well-constrained joint inference of deep temperature and composition. Seismic velocities respond to temperature, pressure, composition, mineral phases and elastic properties, so a velocity anomaly does not identify its cause uniquely. A model can therefore fit seismic observations while assigning an incorrect thermal or chemical explanation. Independent information must distinguish these contributions rather than merely reproduce the same ambiguity in another model.

Observational coverage and material-property uncertainties are separate, interacting barriers. Uneven earthquake locations and receiver distributions limit tomographic resolution; smoothing or incomplete recovery can distort both the magnitude and spatial pattern of inferred temperatures. Translating wave speeds into physical conditions also depends on mineral phase transitions and uncertain elastic and anelastic parameters. Better coverage alone would not remove uncertainties in those relationships, while improved mineral physics alone would not recover structures absent from the observations.

Complementary measurements must supply information at scales relevant to the questions being tested. The reviewed neutrino demonstration constrains coarse radial density structure, which is useful independent information but does not identify detailed chemical variations. For core chemistry, mineral-physics results must be reconciled with cosmochemical and geochemical estimates. The broader engineering challenge is to combine such constraints while retaining their different spatial sensitivities, assumptions and uncertainties.

current_state.text: Seismic tomography already resolves major mantle structures, but converting those structures into temperatures remains uncertain. In their 2025 Geophysical Journal International study, Gabriel Robl and colleagues used a synthetic experiment with known reference temperatures to investigate the conversion from seismic models to mantle temperatures. Even with bulk composition initially assumed known, limited tomographic resolution and mineralogical complexities produced substantial recovery errors. For the tomographic filters tested, the paper reports average temperature errors between 50 and 200 K. These quantify errors within the synthetic experiment; they are not direct measurements of errors against Earth's unknown true temperature field, nor a universal error range for all tomography.

The 2025 study also found that limited resolution and mineralogical uncertainty can distort the spatial patterns of inferred temperature, which matters when those patterns are used in geodynamic reconstructions. Its evidence concerns obstacles to interpreting mantle tomography, rather than a completed global separation of temperature and composition. The supplied review had access to the relevant introduction, methods, discussion and conclusion; the retained extraction was truncated in the references, so it was not a complete extraction of the document.

Andrea Donini, Sergio Palomares-Ruiz and Jordi Salvado's neutrino study, submitted as a preprint on 15 March 2018 and associated in the supplied research with a Nature Physics publication, demonstrated independent density inference from actual neutrino observations. Its model used five concentric layers, fixed core boundaries and one year of IceCube IC86 statistics, with large uncertainties. This establishes a complementary measurement of broad radial density structure, not a spatially detailed chemical or thermal map. The paper's ten-year results were forecasts, not demonstrated later measurements, and the limitations of this particular analysis do not establish the limits of every possible neutrino method. Although the earlier research summary relied on the abstract, the supplied validated review examined an internally identified full-paper extraction.

The review Light elements in the Earth's core, published by Kei Hirose, Bernard Wood and Lidunka Vočadlo on 24 August 2021, described the exact core composition as unknown at that time and combined mineral-physics information with cosmochemical and geochemical estimates. It supports core light elements as an important target for improved constraints. The supplied review could use the verified publisher preview and abstract, but not the full review or figures. Consequently, no numerical abundance ranges are reproduced here. A PDF retained under the same source entry was identified as an unrelated planet-formation paper and provides no evidence about this core-composition review.

Evidence boundary: the supplied material does not substantively establish the research status of the composition and origin of large low-shear-velocity provinces. They remain proposed targets within this concept, without a claim here that any particular interpretation has been established or excluded. The supplied freshness-search record was empty, so these dated sources do not establish developments through 1 November 2026 or show that every specific target remained unresolved then. This limits the currency of the assessment; it does not invalidate the documented 2025 synthetic result or the 2018 neutrino demonstration.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: produce a global three-dimensional model that separately constrains major temperature and compositional variations, with spatial resolution and uncertainty sufficient to distinguish explicitly named geological hypotheses. Before evaluation, specify the hypotheses, target regions and depths, relevant spatial scales, and what differences would count as discriminating evidence. No numerical resolution or error threshold is established by the supplied material; appropriate thresholds would need to follow from the scientific questions rather than being treated as existing standards.
completion_criteria.label: Global temperature and composition constraints distinguish prespecified geological hypotheses

completion_criteria.text: Proposed validation: test whether the model predicts observations withheld from its construction, and compare selected regional conclusions with independent mineral-physics, geochemical and accessible-sample constraints. The need for independent information follows from documented thermal–chemical ambiguity, and the core review illustrates the role of complementary constraints. Withheld prediction and the particular validation design are proposals here. Accessible samples could indirectly test selected interpretations, but could not validate the entire deep interior.
completion_criteria.label: Withheld observations and independent constraints validate selected regional conclusions

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and uncertainty checks: independent teams should be able to recover the central conclusions from documented observations, material-property assumptions and inversion methods. Synthetic recovery experiments should test known thermal and chemical structures under realistic coverage limitations, while sensitivity analyses should show how conclusions change with mineral physics, regularization and other assumptions. Report where uncertainty is calibrated and where it remains dominated by assumptions, rather than presenting one preferred reconstruction as uniquely determined.
completion_criteria.label: Central conclusions are independently reproducible with characterized uncertainty and sensitivity

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundary: success should be claimed for the depths, regions, scales and contrasts that pass these tests. A convincing mantle result would not automatically establish equivalent capability in the core. Finite validation would demonstrate breadth across the tested conditions, not literal universality or exact knowledge of every deep structure. Claims about material movement or heat flow would require additional validation of the dynamical and thermal-transport models used to infer them.
completion_criteria.label: Capability claims remain limited to conditions passing validation tests

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: GEO-01, Reliable short-term forecasting of damaging earthquakes, and GEO-10, Reliable transferable forecasting of volcanic eruptions, overlap through geophysical observations and models of Earth's interior. GEO-02 concerns the physical and chemical state of deep Earth; the forecasting concepts require reliable predictions of particular events on actionable timescales. Improved deep structure could provide context without establishing either forecasting capability.

Roster-based synthesis: GEO-03, Geothermal reservoirs engineered economically in ordinary deep rock, concerns creating usable reservoirs and extracting heat economically. A better thermal model could inform the broader understanding of Earth's heat, but would not establish local reservoir performance or economics. GEO-04, Global-scale, verifiable mineral storage of carbon dioxide, and GEO-06, Discovery of globally consequential recoverable geological hydrogen, share interests in rock chemistry and geological conditions. Their defining outcomes concern storage verification and recoverable resources, respectively, rather than a global deep-interior map.

Roster-based synthesis: GEO-05, Recovery of a detailed geological record of Earth's first half-billion years, and GEO-07, Reconstructing the Moon-forming impact from independent geological evidence, concern historical reconstruction. Deep reservoirs and core chemistry could supply constraints relevant to those histories, but a present-day thermochemical model would not itself recover a detailed early record or uniquely reconstruct an impact. GEO-08, Establishing when and how sustained plate tectonics began, could similarly benefit from constraints on mantle state and dynamics while still requiring evidence that distinguishes historical onset scenarios.

Roster-based synthesis: GEO-09, Predictive laws linking erosion, sediment transport and landscape evolution, concerns surface processes and their evolution. Deep-Earth structure could enter broader accounts of tectonic forcing, but GEO-02 would not establish transferable laws of sediment transport or erosion. All roster entries retain distinct outcomes; possible contributions from deep-interior mapping do not merge their completion criteria.

unresolved_issues: Which geological hypotheses, regions, depths and spatial scales should define the first convincing demonstration, and what uncertainty thresholds would distinguish their predictions?
How can independent constraints separate temperature and composition across both mantle and core without conclusions being dominated by shared assumptions?
The supplied material does not establish the composition or origin of large low-shear-velocity provinces, or the current standing of competing explanations.
The empty freshness-search record prevents an updated assessment through 1 November 2026; later progress cannot be inferred from the dated sources.
Full text and figures of the 2021 core review were unavailable in the supplied review, so detailed compositional ranges and their qualifications remain unverified here.
The neutrino study's projected ten-year performance is not established as an achieved result by the supplied evidence.

brief.title: A map of temperature and materials deep inside Earth
possible: Scientists could distinguish deep regions that are hotter or colder from regions made of different materials. A global map showing these differences at depth, with clear limits on its accuracy, would let them test competing explanations of what lies beneath us.
why: For scientists reconstructing Earth’s past, separating temperature from chemistry would sharpen explanations of buried material and why some regions rise while others sink. Temperature errors can otherwise distort those accounts.
Knowing the core’s ingredients more precisely would help scientists explain how Earth formed and what sustains its magnetic field.

sources.showed: In a computer experiment, they tried to recover known temperatures from simulated earthquake-wave maps. Limited detail and uncertain mineral properties distorted the recovered temperatures, even with the overall chemistry assumed known.
sources.quote:
Fur ther more, large systematic errors exist in the vicinity 
of phase transitions due to the associated mineralogical complexities.
sources.cited_for: Mapping earthquake-wave speeds does not reliably reveal temperature on its own.
sources.not_established: The experiment did not separate temperature and chemistry throughout the real Earth.

sources.who: Andrea Donini, Sergio Palomares-Ruiz and Jordi Salvado
sources.showed: They used neutrinos, tiny particles that pass through Earth, to estimate density in broad layers from IceCube observations. Their estimates had large uncertainties.
sources.quote:
We are able to determine the mass of the Earth, its
moment of inertia, the mass of the Earth’s core and to establish the core is denser than the mantle,
using weak interactions only, in a way completely independent from gravitational measurements.
sources.cited_for: Particle observations can provide density information independent of earthquake waves.
sources.not_established: Broad density estimates do not reveal detailed temperature or chemical variations.

sources.who: Kei Hirose, Bernard Wood and Lidunka Vočadlo
sources.showed: Their review combined studies of mineral properties with estimates from Earth and space chemistry to narrow the possible mixtures of elements in the core.
sources.quote: Earth’s outer and inner core exhibit a density deficit relative to pure iron, attributed to the presence of substantial amounts of low atomic number ‘light’ elements, such as sulfur, silicon, oxygen, carbon and hydrogen.
sources.cited_for: Core chemistry is an important target that requires several kinds of constraint.
sources.not_established: The review did not establish the core’s exact composition.

shown: Earthquake-wave maps already reveal major structures in the mantle, the rocky layer surrounding the core. Researchers also have independent estimates of broad density structure and possible core ingredients. These pieces have yet to become a global map that reliably distinguishes temperature from chemistry.
missing: A global model must distinguish temperature, chemistry and changes in mineral structure rather than assign the wrong cause to wave-speed differences.
Observations must resolve the structures being tested, while mineral measurements must reliably connect wave speeds to physical conditions.
Independent measurements must constrain the same regions and scales closely enough to separate competing explanations.

milestones.label: A global map distinguishes competing geological explanations
milestones.explanation: A global model would have to separate temperature and chemistry well enough to distinguish explanations chosen beforehand at specified depths and scales. This would demonstrate useful discrimination.

milestones.label: Unused observations and independent tests support regional conclusions
milestones.explanation: The model would have to predict observations left out of its construction and agree with independent mineral, chemistry and accessible rock-sample tests. This would test whether selected regional conclusions hold up.

milestones.label: Independent teams reproduce conclusions and characterize uncertainty
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to recover central conclusions, test known simulated structures and measure sensitivity to assumptions. This would reveal which findings survive uncertainty in observations and mineral properties.

milestones.label: Capability claims stay within tested conditions
milestones.explanation: Claims would have to stay within tested regions, depths, scales and contrasts, with further validation for inferred movement or heat flow. This would keep success in one setting from implying success everywhere.

uncertain: Which geological explanations and spatial scales should define success, and how small must uncertainty be to distinguish them?
Can independent measurements separate temperature and chemistry across both mantle and core without relying on the same uncertain assumptions?

page.title: Global thermochemical tomography of Earth’s mantle and core
page.definition: A global three-dimensional model separates temperature, chemical composition and mineral-phase effects in Earth’s mantle and core, with quantified uncertainty and spatial resolution. Thermochemical tomography infers these properties jointly from geophysical observations and material properties measured or calculated at high pressure and temperature.

goal.need: In a 2025 synthetic mantle experiment with known bulk composition, recovered temperatures had depth-dependent RMS errors of 50–100 K in the upper mantle, reaching 200 K near the core–mantle boundary for some tomographic filters. These are recovery errors, not measurements of Earth’s unknown temperature errors. A 2021 review placed published core-side boundary-temperature estimates between 3,400 and 4,600 K. Separating temperature from chemistry is necessary to interpret inferred density and buoyancy.

figures.caption: Temperature-recovery errors in the 2025 synthetic mantle experiment
rows: Up to 200 K for some tomographic filters
figures.note: Bulk composition was assumed known. These values are neither acceptance thresholds nor measured errors against Earth’s true temperature field.

statements.body: Seismological Grand Challenges Writing Group, in the IRIS report to the National Science Foundation
statements.quote: What are the relative contributions of thermal, chemical, and mineralogical variations to seismically detected heterogeneity?

statements.context: The project objective concerns the lithosphere and upper mantle.

completion.title: A global mantle-and-core model separates temperature, composition and mineral-phase effects.
completion.criterion: A global three-dimensional model of the mantle and core jointly constrains temperature and chemical composition, with spatial resolution and joint uncertainties sufficient to distinguish thermal, chemical and mineral-phase explanations of observed heterogeneity. Separation is supported by observations with different sensitivities, remains identifiable when material-property uncertainties are propagated, and is reproduced by an independent analysis. Coverage and resolved scales are explicit. No universal numerical accuracy or spatial-resolution threshold is specified.
completion.set_by: Atlas fallback; no external whole-interior completion test was located.
completion.basis: Searches of the IRIS grand-challenge report, WINTERC-3D objectives, published thermochemical inversion acceptance rules and synthetic-recovery benchmarks found no whole-interior completion test or common accuracy/resolution threshold. This test retains the published objective of separating thermal, chemical and mineralogical contributions. Existing upper- and lower-mantle inferences do not establish this combined mantle-and-core capability.

milestones.title: Laboratory experiments measure mineral sound velocities at controlled high pressure and temperature.
milestones.criterion: Obtain in-situ sound-speed measurements for a mineral of known composition while pressure and temperature are controlled, using established light-scattering or ultrasonic methods. The 2020 technical review documents polycrystalline ferropericlase and bridgmanite measurements at about 95 GPa and 2,700 K: seven data points, four for ferropericlase and three for bridgmanite. It also identifies substantial temperature uncertainty and incomplete material coverage.
milestones.set_by: Mineral-physics community convention, documented by Marquardt and Thomson’s technical review; the quoted formulation concerns mantle minerals.
milestones.threshold_quote: experimental in-situ measurements of sound wave velocities of mantle minerals at high-pressure/-temperature

milestones.title: A global upper-mantle thermochemical model combines seismic, gravity and elevation observations.
milestones.criterion: Produce a global lithosphere-and-upper-mantle temperature/composition model using seismic waveform information, satellite gravity and surface elevation within a self-consistent thermodynamic framework. WINTERC-G, published on 10 March 2021, reports such an inversion, additionally incorporating heat flow. Its seismic inputs came from 6,242 stations and 25,496 earthquakes. Its 225 km average knot spacing describes model parametrization, not independently demonstrated resolving power. The programme supplied no numerical accuracy threshold.
milestones.set_by: European Commission, Horizon 2020 WINTERC-3D, grant 657357, published project objective; scope is the lithosphere and upper mantle.
milestones.threshold_quote: a robust and, at the same time, detailed thermochemical model of the Earth’s lithosphere and upper mantle.

milestones.title: A lower-mantle inversion fits seismic data using reference properties within 1% of PREM.
milestones.criterion: Apply Mosca et al.’s inversion rule: reference assemblages match the Preliminary Reference Earth Model (PREM), a radial seismic reference, in bulk modulus, shear modulus and density within 1%. Perturbed perovskite plus post-perovskite and iron volumes remain within 12% and 6%, respectively, of reference values. Accepted temperature/composition perturbations jointly fit tomographic probability distributions of P-wave speed, S-wave speed and density. The study published on 7 June 2012 mapped six lower-mantle depths; temperature and silicate variations remained unconstrained in the lowest few hundred kilometres.
milestones.set_by: Mosca et al., published probabilistic-inversion acceptance rules, section 5, paragraphs 39–42; a lower-mantle study protocol, not a field-wide accuracy standard.
milestones.threshold_quote: We impose the constraint that elastic bulk and shear moduli as well as density in the reference models must fit PREM within 1%.

milestones.title: One global mantle-and-core thermochemical model fits seismic and independent density constraints.
milestones.criterion: A single three-dimensional mantle-and-core temperature/composition model predicts its seismic and independent density observations within their stated observational and modelling uncertainties, although thermal–chemical trade-offs may remain. Partial independent-density evidence exists: the manuscript submitted on 15 March 2018 inferred five concentric density layers from 20,145 IceCube muons recorded over 343.7 days, with fixed core boundaries. That analysis did not infer three-dimensional temperature or composition.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback; searches of community objectives and joint-inversion studies located no externally specified whole-interior precursor test.

not_found: No published whole-interior model meeting the stated discrimination test was located.
The WINTERC-3D final-report page could not be opened; its project objective and the WINTERC-G paper were accessible.
